text:
Ashley K: quick heads-up, perf regression after yesterday's kernel selector change. seeing a cluster of OOMs on long-prompt paged-attn runs when batch sizes spike. trace attached: high compaction CPU time and a bunch of tiny allocations.

Raj P: :eyes: which change? the selector patch that prefers faiss-like kernels? commit 9a7c2f1?

Ashley K: yeah that's the one. selector now prefers kernel_v2 for small seq lengths which is faster normally, but with paged-attn + KV cache churn it leads to more split-block allocations. gist of the perf summary: 
```
- 95th latency: +12%
- compaction CPU time: +3.2s per 1000 reqs
- allocations: many 4KB->16KB splinters
- frequent KV eviction watermark crosses causing additional mallocs
```

Marta S: high-level guess: kernel_v2 has a different workspace footprint and when batch probe kicks in it probes with small allocations instead of using existing block reuse path. that increases fragmentation and forces compaction earlier.

Leo C: I saw similar in the profiler: flamegraph shows repeated hot path around blockmgr::alloc_small + compact_if_needed. posted snapshot: https://perf.internal/runs/2129/flame (only team) :thinking_face:

Raj P: could be two levers: 1) adjust batch_probe_threshold so we don't probe that many times for transient spikes, 2) increase kv_eviction_high_watermark to give blocks time to be reused before eviction.

Ashley K: tried a quick experiment. raised dynamic_reserve_ratio from 0.12 -> 0.22 on a canary, and reduced probe rate with batch_probe_interval_ms 50 -> 120. results: OOMs dropped 86%, tail latency back to baseline, compaction time down ~1.8s. but cost of keeping more reserved memory increased per-token GPU memory utilization. tradeoff confirmed.

Marta S: interesting. can we do smarter reuse heuristic instead? e.g., prefer reusing slab-aligned blocks for mini-allocs created by kernel_v2 and avoid splitting larger blocks unless idle for X ms. pseudo: 
```
if (alloc_size <= SLAB_MIN && last_free_age < REUSE_WINDOW) {
  reuse_from_slab();
} else {
  fallback_alloc();
}
```

Leo C: also worth measuring compaction CPU cost vs reclaimed bytes. compaction has diminishing returns if it runs too often for small frees. we might set compaction_min_reclaim_bytes = 64KB to avoid thrash.

Raj P: agree. plan: 1) revert the kernel selector tweak for traffic > 1.5K qps until we land a reuse patch, 2) run A/B with dynamic_reserve_ratio 0.12/0.22, 3) add instrumentation to count split vs reuse events per blocksize.

Ashley K: I'll open a short-lived feature-flagged change for the selector revert + counters. ticket INV-4321 created with perf traces and sample cfg. assigning myself to the revert, Marta for reuse heuristic prototype, Raj to run the canary A/B job.

infra-bot: deploy registered: rollout/kv-watermark-revert canary started (build 5482) :rocket:

Marta S: prototype note — might be easier to implement reuse_window in blockmgr rather than kernel-level hacks. will sketch tomorrow and push a draft branch.

Leo C: once we have counters, let's add a nightly job to surface split/reuse ratio and compaction cost per model so we alert earlier for regressions.

Ashley K: sounds good. short-term: monitor canary, PR for revert up in ~30m. long-term: reuse heuristic + compaction tuning. thanks all :thumbsup:
